newsitem.title: USA: Haggar consolidates Texas sewing units.
newsitem.headline: Haggar consolidates Texas sewing units.

text.p: Haggar Clothing Co said Monday it will consolidate the Edinburg, Texas, and Weslaco, Texas, sewing operations into its Edinburg facility as part of its restructuring plans to reduce manufacturing costs.
The company, an operating subsidiary of Haggar Corp, said it will also cease sewing operations in Weslaco.

"This step concludes the consolidation of our three Texas sewing operations into one facility, and the restructuring of the domestic portion of our world-wide manufacturing capacity, which we announced in October 1996," it said.

"The restructuring plan potentially reduces manufacturing costs by $12 million to $14 million on a full year basis, and the charge for accomplishing the restructuring was taken during the fourth quarter of fiscal year 1996, which ended September 30, 1996," it added.
The company said the Edinburg facility will produce men's pants as well as some coat production that was once done at the Weslaco plant.
It said it will transfer about 175 Weslaco employees, while offering another 500 to other facilities. A severance package would be offered to those who declined to go elsewhere, it added.
"Haggar's cutting facility, packing center and material warehouse located in Weslaco will remain unaffected by this restructuring," the company said.
Haggar Clothing Co makes men's casual and dress wear.
